 Order

. This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail, as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 52/2023 registered at Police Station - Nagarda, District - Sakti, Chhattisgarh for the offences punishable under Section 323, 363,
366, 376 (2) (I) (N), 376 (R) of IPC, 1860 and under Section 3, 4 (2) and 5 (L) of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
2. Case of the prosecution is that, the co-accused Chandra Kumar Lahre had forcefully abducted the victim and took her to different place along with other persons on a train to Mahka and from there,
he took the victim on a motorcycle to the house of his sister and brother-in-law where, he committed forceful sexual intercourse with her.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is an allegation that the applicant and her husband used to ask the victim to sleep in the room of the co-accused Chandra Kumar Lahre and further, she was forced to marry the co- accused Chandra Kumar Lahre.
After sometime, when she obtained Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1863 mobile phone of other persons, gave a mobile call to her sister and her sister informed the fact to her father.
Thereafter, the mother of the applicant and the co-accused Tulsi took the victim to her house and from there, victim was recovered.
After recording her statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the aforementioned crime was registered against the co-accused persons and the applicant was arrested on 25.09.2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any offence as alleged.
He submits that the allegation of abducting and committing forceful sexual intercourse if any, would be against the co-accused Chandra Kumar Lahre who is brother of the applicant.

From the charge-sheet, it is appearing that the victim along with the co-accused Chandra Kumar Lahre resided in the house of the applicant, except the said fact, there is no other material against the applicant.

4. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the applicant and would submit that the victim in the statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and the statement that the victim and the co-accused Tulsi used to send her to sleep in the room of the co-accused Chandra Kumar Lahre and further, applicant and co-accused Tulsi had forced her to marry co-accused Chandra Kumar.
She also submits that as per the documents enclosed along with the bail application, it is appearing that the victim had stood with the allegations before the Learned Trial Court also.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties.

6. Taking in consideration the submission of counsel for the parties and in particular, submission of the counsel for the State based on the statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1863 also the Court statement, I do not find present to be a fit case for allowing the application to enlarge the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is rejected at this stage.

Sd/-
